children: High-quality U.S. Treasuries are again paying investors to wait. On Tuesday, the U.S. 2 Year Treasury yield
yielded 4.74%, the benchmark U.S. 10 Year Treasury yield
traded near 4.94%, and the U.S. 30 Year Treasury yield

Those levels mark a sharp break from the decade when policy rates sat near zero and income-seekers were forced into weaker credits. Apollo Global Management's chief economist, Torsten Slok, called the current backdrop “starting to look juicy.”
Households and institutions with long-duration liabilities no longer need to stretch for yield; investment-grade government paper already delivers competitive cash flow.

Slok argued that even if yields rise from here, starting points this high already look attractive. After years of reaching for return, savers can lock in income without leaving the safest part of the fixed-income market. A modestly upward-sloping curve now supplies carry that was simply unavailable when short-term rates were pinned at the floor.
For asset allocators, the combination of elevated coupons and sovereign credit quality is the story. The zero-rate hunt is over; quality itself is paying again.

title: Apollo says yields are starting to look ‘juicy’ again
